proof.surface: scripts/e2e/parked-decision-devbox.sh's own rig and boot (start_listener, start_dispatch, write_legion_config, install-plugin-profile.sh, install-key-file-model-route.sh, the real `legion start`) in this issue's pod, with Postgres 18 and NATS 2.10 started locally, a scratch Dispatch project PDBOOT mapped to sjawhar/legion-smoke, and a stand-in mise for the pinned Oh My Pi build (the pod has no mise or tmux)
proof.command: script edit: require_app_inputs implement; write_github_apps implement; the implement entry copied to the review slot; check_github_apps implement. Then legion start --check-config --config work/legion.yaml; then start_kept daemon … legion start --config work/legion.yaml
proof.observed: GET /app proved the key: {"implement":"legion-implementer[bot]"}, both slots app_id "5341240". `legion start --check-config` printed 'Config OK: project=PDBOOT'. The real boot passed the plugin gate ('pi-legion speaks this daemon's contract and loads with pi-envoy', daemonApiVersion 44) and the store, config and dispatch stages, then exited: 'legion start: the review App names bot login "legion-implementer[bot]" and the implement App "legion-implementer[bot]"; the workflow needs two different Apps' (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/workflow.go:233, appLoginsAtBoot, called at workflow.go:294; workflow_test.go:90 asserts it). The daemon judges a push by its pusher against the review App's login, so one App cannot serve both roles. The architect ruled: no daemon change and no other App; the script stays as it is (two Apps) and the proof waits on a readable key for the review App 5341243.
proof.negativeControl: `legion start --check-config` accepts the one-App file (it runs no key command and reads no login), so it cannot show the refusal; only the real boot reaches appLoginsAtBoot, and the refusal names both logins.
